memos.scout:
The strongest case for buying COOK is the last 15 minutes: 960 buyers put in 682 SOL against 619 SOL sold, a 94% return, and 169 sellers suggests real two-sided trading rather than a single wash loop. The coin is not an airdrop factory (airdrop_dump_seen is false), it is alive, and it has held a 13% gain over 30 minutes after a 12% pullback from its high, with $156k of volume in 15 minutes and roughly $197k market cap. Pool depth of 173 SOL is adequate for a $20 ticket.

The case is weaker than it looks. The bundle_share of 1.0 and top3_share of 0.90 mean the early curve was dominated by coordinated buying, and the top5 buyers took 61% of post-graduation SOL, which is the operator-backed pattern that has been roughly break-even. Sell-to-buy in the first two minutes was 0.48. I cannot say from this brief whether recent demand will persist 30-60 minutes out, so this is a marginal, not a strong, buy.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: insider distribution into the 30-minute recovery. The curve is almost entirely bundled (bundle_share 1.0, top3 holders 89.5%, completer_share 1.40, meaning the completing buyer alone bought more than the supply sold), so whoever bundled the launch controls most of the float. The last 15 minutes show 94% return, but net flow is only +63 SOL on 682 SOL bought, with 619 SOL sold and sellers (169) and buyers (960) far apart. The 11.6% drawdown from the 30-minute high is the first sign of exits starting. A 1.4-5.1% round trip on a $20 ticket is thin margin against a 2-digit dump. Pool depth of 173 SOL means sizable sells move price hard. Skip.
